paraphrase: The body is made of the five elements, rests on six supports, has six flavours, seven constituents, three humours and two kinds of birth.

checks.note: E-text 1 located in the e-text; the passage matches the paraphrase.

paraphrase: The embryo grows month by month: after one night a mixture, seven nights a bubble, a fortnight a lump, a month firm; head in the second month, feet in the third, and so on; in the ninth it is complete.

checks.note: The e-text divides the Garbha into five numbered sections. Section 2 covers the six flavours, seven colours and seven dhātus. The month-by-month growth of the embryo (ekarātroṣitaṃ kalilam … navame māse sarvasampūrṇaḥ) is section 3.

paraphrase: Excess of the father's seed gives a male, of the mother's a female, equal a eunuch; defects arise from the parents' state.

checks.note: Male, female and eunuch according to excess of seed (pitū reto'tiriktāt puruṣaḥ …), and defects from the parents' state (vyākulitamanaso'ndhāḥ …), are in e-text section 3.

paraphrase: In the ninth month the embryo remembers its past births and vows: if freed from the womb it will resort to Sāṃkhya-yoga, to Maheśvara or Nārāyaṇa, and meditate on Brahman; touched at birth by the Vaiṣṇava wind, it forgets.

checks.note: The content spans e-text sections 3-4: 'navame māsi … pūrvajātīḥ smarati' closes section 3, and the lament, the vows and the Vaiṣṇava wind (vaiṣṇavena vāyunā saṃspṛṣṭaḥ) end section 4.

paraphrase: Counts of the body: 107 vital points, 180 joints, 109 sinews, 700 veins, 360 bones, and so on.

checks.note: E-text section 5 is located: the etymology of śarīra (three fires) and the counts (saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ, sāśītikaṃ sandhiśatam …).
